page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided by a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2503.49 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 36.27 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 20287.03 and a Passmark CPU score of 23271.22. Memory performance exhibits a notable tradeoff: while the Passmark memory score is in the top tier at 3390.33 and cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 1099.44 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are weak, measuring 36.93 GB/sec and 19.38 GB/sec respectively.

Given its high memory capacity relative to CPU cores and its large local NVMe storage, this server offers a resource-dense profile suitable for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, as evidenced by an average Passmark database score of 8480.87 and a Redis SET performance of 16.84 million operations per second. Additionally, it supports moderate LLM text generation, achieving 275.61 tokens per second on a small 135M model. The combination of dedicated bare-metal resources and high-capacity NVMe storage makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring isolated CPU execution and local data persistence without the overhead of virtualization.

It includes 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage but lacks GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, highlighted by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and strong single-core stress-ng results. However, uncached large-block memory bandwidth remains a bottleneck, scoring in the lower tier. With a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core and substantial local storage, this server is optimized for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, and localized data processing. It delivers reliable, isolated performance for workloads such as Redis caching, database operations, and web serving without virtualization overhead.
